own.claim: A same-day or next-day reply to a warm inbound investor inquiry keeps the thread hot and signals seriousness.
own.why: Investors see many companies and move on quickly; a delayed reply reads as low priority or low responsiveness, both of which matter in early-stage fundraising.

own.claim: Angel investors who reference a specific product demo are more likely to move to a call than those who have only read materials.
own.why: A demo is a higher-friction engagement than a deck; it signals the investor has already spent time and formed an opinion.

own.claim: The deck and meeting slot should be sent together in a single reply, with the meeting options pre-filled to reduce friction.
own.why: Each back-and-forth delays momentum; offering three specific time slots removes the coordination cost and signals respect for the investor's time.

own.claim: An angel investor asking for a deck without a prior introduction or warm connector is more likely to be a low-conviction inquiry or a portfolio-building exercise.
own.why: Serious investors often come through warm intros or have already done preliminary diligence; a cold ask for a deck can indicate a low bar for engagement.

patterns.claim: Inbound investor inquiries that name a specific ask and a time window convert at higher rates than outbound cold waves.
